messages:
opsbot: INCIDENT detected: continuous-batching latency cliff on us-west cluster. Alerts from both frontend and runtime dashboards. Auto-pager triggered. severity=P2. affected_service=continuous-batcher, affected_subsystem=kvcache

alex: got the page, looking. seeing huge KV eviction spikes + queue depth increasing on batchers. CPU on GPUs fine, but tail latency for token generation jumping ~10x. first hypothesis: eviction spiral causing microbatch starvation -> queues back up -> larger microbatches -> more kv pressure.

mira: confirmed on model-prod/llama-70b-quant. 90th pct token latency is 4.2s -> 40s in some pods. error rate (502/timeout) up to 6% for requests hitting the dedicated pool. customer-impact: a handful of mid-market customers on Dedicated capacity experiencing timeouts.

samir: attaching quick metrics I pulled:
```
# kvcache stats snapshot
kvcache.size_bytes: 1.9TB
kvcache.evictions_1m: 12k
microbatch.avg_size: 8 -> jumped to 24
queue.depth: 150 -> 1200
continuous.batch.latency_p95: 4.2s -> 38s
```
Looks like continuous batching config's target microbatch got blown out under high concurrency + jitter, and eviction rate jumped (TTL+LRU thrash).

rachel: are we seeing any config rollouts recently? I don't see a scheduled config push but there was an autoscale change last night. Could be traffic pattern change + prefix cache miss storm.

alex: ops checklist: 1) throttle new requests to the affected pool; 2) revert recent batch-adaptive tuning (if any); 3) enable temporary eviction cap; 4) contact customers with ETA. I'm going to flip a temporary throttle on the pool and open a mitigation PR.

emma: +1 on throttle. please post exact rollback commands. i can handle comms to the affected accounts.

samir: rollback command (runtime):
```
# reduce batch target and disable adaptive growth
curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/api/v1/pools/us-west/llama-70b/patch -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEYS' 
-d '{"batching": {"target_microbatch": 8, "adaptive": false}}'
```
Then cap kv eviction workers:
```
curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/api/v1/kvcache/patch -d '{"eviction": {"max_rate_per_sec": 2000}}'
```
I'll also increase pool concurrency limit to avoid queue pileups: set concurrency_limit to 600 -> 400? (we want lower concurrent inflight to avoid queueing explosion).

alex: executed the batch patch and eviction cap. watching metrics. so far queue.depth dropping from 1200 -> 450 in ~2min. tail latency trending down to ~12s. error rate falling.

mira: re microbatch jitter: we should also enable prefix caching for this model variant for the hot prefixes seen in logs. i'm pushing a temporary cache-whitelist for top 50 prefixes.

rachel: taking notes for post-incident: need clearer SLOs for eviction rate and a circuit breaker when microbatch > 16. also add anomaly alert for microbatch growth > 3x baseline.

opsbot: PAGE Escalation: oncall->eng-runtime after 15m if recovery not below thresholds.

alex: quick customer impact summary for comms:
- scope: Dedicated us-west pool serving llama-70b-quant variants; ~3% of total requests hit the affected backend; ~4 customers observed timeouts (isolated).
- mitigation: throttled new accepts on pool, reverted adaptive batching, capped eviction rate, enabled prefix whitelist caching; result: queue depth dropped 70%, p95 latency down from 38s -> 9s in 10min.

emma: sending customer note now: short outage explanation + ETA for full remediation (we'll follow up postmortem).

samir: follow-up actions I'm taking now: 1) implement a soft circuit breaker at microbatch > 16 to reject/route to fallback model; 2) add eviction backpressure to batcher so eviction storms don't cascade; 3) add metric emit for adaptive growth events.

mira: i'll run a local replay of the traffic spike against a staging bucket to validate soft-circuit behavior. leaving a runbook snippet in the incident doc.

alex: handoff to daytime oncall (rachel) in 30m. current state: stable, but not fully healed — we've reduced tail latency considerably but need to validate prefix whitelist and soft-circuit in staging before scaling back throttles.

rachel: ack, i'll own post-incident follow-ups and the postmortem. will schedule a 1-hour blameless review and include runtime, ml, and sde-oncall.

opsbot: INCIDENT update: severity -> P3 (reduced), ongoing monitoring for 2 hours.

alex: small log snippet for the PM:
```
[2026-04-11T16:48:22Z] batcher: microbatch_size=24, inflight=520, kv_evictions=1200/s
[2026-04-11T16:50:10Z] config: applied batch_patch target_microbatch=8 adaptive=false by alex
[2026-04-11T16:54:03Z] kvcache: eviction_rate capped=2000/s
```

mira: thanks all. next steps list in incident doc: triage cause of adaptive growth, tune soft-circuit thresholds, add alerting, postmortem + customer follow-up.

alex: handing off. ping me if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
